correctness.rationale: First-order rank types obey T_{s+1}(a)=(atomic(a),{T_s(a,x):x vertex}). Ordered triples of vertices have coordinate equality-pattern orbits 000,001,010,011,012 (012 forbidden q=2); nonadjacency depends on pairwise distances clipped at two. Choosing an extra word amounts to additive clipped-distance transitions on all 27 states. Verified exact stationarity from every possible initial 27-state vector after caps: for binary 000 cap2 and split patterns cap4; for nonbinary 000 cap2 and others cap3. Child-coordinate splitting of pair types saturates at (6,8) for q=2 and (5,9) for q>=3, reducing all dimensions >=14 to the same pair-type set. Independently reimplemented and exhaustively compared exact nested types, not digest hashes, for q=2,3,4 and d=1..14 (42 boundary cases); obtained exactly 16 classes, binary saturation d=6 and ternary/quaternary d=5 with no cross-regime coincidences. q>=4 has identical extension options for tuples of at most three chosen vertices. The minimal H(5,4) class has 4^5=1024 vertices. Finite calculation is exhaustive only because of the analytic orbit/transition/saturation reductions.

value.rationale: A complete logical classification for every dimension and alphabet size in a natural distance-regular graph family, distinguishing unusual binary versus nonbinary cutoffs and giving a sharp finite representative for testing every rank-four first-order sentence. This is not simply graph isomorphism, automorphism or VC-dimension classification.

final_claim: H(d,q) in pure adjacency/equality rank-four first-order logic has exactly 16 equivalence classes: q=2 with dimensions capped at 6, q=3 and q>=4 each with dimensions capped at 5; H(5,4) is the largest smallest representative, on 1024 vertices.
limitations: Pure unlabeled adjacency/equality first-order rank <=4 only; no counting quantifiers, named coordinates, rank-five characterization or classification of arbitrary induced subgraphs. Binary-only subcase previously known; exact 16-class originality remains qualified.
